walkthroughs.body_html:
Two prisoners, separate cells.

Stay silent (Cooperate) or confess (Defect)? Years in jail:
(C,C)=(1,1); (D,D)=(5,5); (C,D)=(10,0); (D,C)=(0,10).

Defect is dominant for each — yet joint Defect (5,5) is worse than joint Cooperate (1,1). Individual rationality → collective loss.

A strategy is strictly dominant if it gives a higher payoff than any other, whatever the rival does.

It is strictly dominated if another strategy is always better.

Method: iterated elimination of dominated strategies can simplify games to a unique Nash equilibrium.

OPEC members face a prisoner's dilemma. Each gains by cheating quotas — but if all cheat, the price collapses.

Solution attempts: repeated games, audits, monitoring, side payments. Tit-for-tat (Axelrod 1984) can sustain cooperation if the game repeats indefinitely.
